reports.summary: No tenant can be reused for Part B. No database has a tenant holding mt5k's 5,089 documents. The only full-bank tenant with the 5,000-document base (seed 5) is erbfull-5000-9688c2 in cie_erb. It holds exactly the 5,000 base documents (mt5k minus its 89 metadata/conflict gold documents), but it cannot be used as it is, for four reasons. (1) cie_erb is two migrations behind (f8a9b0c1d2e3; the repo head is b0c1d2e3f4a5): it still has 32-bit vectors and stored tsv columns, and lacks the cie_record_tsv and cie_section_tsv functions that today's code calls. With today's code, a bank search on any question containing a quoted phrase would raise an error and leave the bank's evidence empty. That is 58 of the 115 usable questions and 14 of the 50 fb50 questions. (2) The bench_loop runs (Sep 29 to Oct 3) wrote 4,580 records into this tenant that are not from the haystack; 3,167 of them sit in company, department or project scopes that the admin search sees. (3) Only 22 of the 50 fb50 questions and 115 of the 219 eligible mt5k questions have all their gold documents in the 5,000, and only 11 of those are owners questions. (4) It was loaded with the Sep 23 code. That load gives the same section and record texts as today: a sample of 40 base documents hit the embedding cache 464 of 464 times. Only the storage format differs, plus display_title (not used by Part B's arms). The workable path is a new load of mt5k (5,089 documents) into the current schema (cie_pb, the database the 50-document run used), followed by building the plain index and collecting evidence. Copying the 84 MB embedding cache from the 5,000-document runs makes the bank load cheap (about 3 to 8 minutes). The plain index's vectors cannot use that cache: about 36,000 passages take about 35 to 42 minutes. Disk is the binding limit: 1.8 GB is free, and the projected peak is 1.2 to 1.7 GB. All times are extrapolated from earlier logs; I ran nothing heavy.

findings.title: (1) Exact commands and what each needs
findings.detail:
Part B's inputs in one work folder W: haystack.json, index.json, questions.jsonl, load.json, plain/ with plain_meta.json, evidence.jsonl, evidence_info.json (its storage), factbank.sqlite, factbank_build.json, factbank.jsonl. Steps:
(a) Work folder. factbank_test.select cannot make it, because it hard-codes N_DOCS=50. Assemble it by hand, as the u5k probe did: copy mt5k/haystack.json, symlink mt5k/index.json, and copy the chosen questions.jsonl.
(b) `memory_test load`. Runs ensure_indexes, then find_loaded_tenant(dsids, 'full'), which looks only for a tenant named erbfull-5089-* in CIE_DATABASE_URL whose documents equal the haystack. Finding none, it calls bench_enterprise.load_full: worker processes (default CPUs minus 1, so 3), batches of 64, a CachedEmbedder at (local or work)/emb_cache.sqlite, links, near-duplicates and entity profiles, then the tenant's BM25 (tantivy) index under CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR. Needs Postgres with pgvector 0.7 or newer (cie_pb has 0.8.1) at alembic head; CIE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fastembed, whose model BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 is cached in cie/.models (the relative ./.models, so run from cie/); CIE_LLM_PROVIDER=none. /tmp/fastembed_cache holds only rerankers that no repo code uses, so it is not needed.
(c) `memory_test plain`. Reads the raw documents, cuts 1,000-character passages (bench_enterprise.chunk over render_doc), builds a tantivy BM25 index and fp16 vectors with the same fastembed model, called directly with no cache. Writes W/plain/{chunks.jsonl,bm25/,vectors.npy,meta.json} and W/plain_meta.json. --no-vectors builds BM25 only, and the 'plain' arm then silently falls back to words only.
(d) `memory_test evidence --arms plain-words,plain,bank`. Needs load.json (tenant and company id, admin principal), the plain index, the same DB and the same CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR (storage() reads the tenant's BM25 directory), and fastembed for query vectors. No LLM.
(e) `factbank_test build`, then `ask`, then `score`. SQLite only, no DB. score's to_markdown title hard-codes '50 documents'.
The 50-document run used CIE_DATABASE_URL=cie_pb (tenant erbfull-50-c6dd93) and CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR=<scratchpad>/fb_lexical. No retrieval, memory, ingest or memory_test code has changed since that run's commit (8375901), so the bank and plain evidence code is identical; only the fact bank code changed.
findings.numbers: cie_pb at alembic b0c1d2e3f4a5 = repo head; all 8 shared indexes present on the new layout (HNSW on halfvec, GIN on cie_*_tsv); lexical_engine default bm25, lexical_tail_max 20,000

No database (cie, cie_erb, cie_mt, cie_pb, cie_nb, cie_colab, cie_scale, cie_test) has a tenant with 5,089 documents. Questions with all gold documents inside the 5,000: 135 of 243 mt5k questions, and 115 of the 219 the fact-bank test can use (owners 11, deadlines 68, lists 36). Of fb50's 50 questions, 22 are inside (deadlines 16, lists 5, owners 1); 28 are outside (owners 25, deadlines 2, lists 1). The 85 owners questions outside are exactly the metadata questions whose gold is among the 89. For list questions whose gold is all inside, the expected answer over the 5,000 is unchanged, because the list members are the gold documents.

findings.title: (3) The 5,000 tenant was not built with today's code and is contaminated
findings.detail: Created 2026-09-23 18:44 UTC, at commit db60fff. Since then, 5 commits touched src/cie/memory or src/cie/ingest and 13 touched src/cie/retrieval. Changes that affect a load: ingest/bulk.py now writes halfvec, stores no tsv, and adds display_title to documents.extra; the builder and sources code is unchanged. Today's builder gives the same section and record texts: 464 of 464 cache hits on 40 sampled base documents. cie_erb is at f8a9b0c1d2e3 and misses a9b0c1d2e3f4 (compact_storage: halfvec columns, tsv dropped, GIN on cie_*_tsv functions) and b0c1d2e3f4a5 (playbooks). In cie_erb the embedding columns are vector(384) with HNSW on embedding::halfvec, and today's vector.py does handle that layout as halfvec_expr. But `SELECT cie_record_tsv(...)` fails there with 'function does not exist', and exact.lookup calls it outside run_bounded for every question with a quoted phrase or clause number. retrieve() would raise, and collect_evidence would record bank_error with empty bank evidence: 58 of the 115 usable questions and 14 of fb50's 50. The full-text fallback would also fail, though run_bounded swallows that error. BM25 is ready for this tenant in cie/.cie_data/lexical/410f29d0... (15 MB, built Sep 30), with 3,685 queued rows waiting, below the 20,000 limit. Contamination: bench_loop wrote 1,781 'loop-bench-loader' facts and 2,799 'operations' results (Sep 29 to Oct 3, all without a source document), 1,386 extra links, 194 agent scopes and more project and department scopes. 3,167 of those records are in company (796), department (178) or project (2,193) scopes that an admin search at company scope reaches; the 1,413 in agent scopes are hidden by default.

findings.title: (3) Cost of a new local load of mt5k (5,089 documents)
findings.detail:
Earlier logs: the 5,000-document full load (erb_full_5k.log, Sep 23) took 905.2 s, of which 817.9 s was embedding 14,868 new texts (47,093 came from the cache). That is 55 ms per text (18 texts/s) with 3 workers, and about 87 s for everything other than embedding (about 17 ms per document). Sections plus records came to 61,922 texts for 5,000 documents (12.4 per document). The fb50 load: 71.4 s for 50 documents, 49.7 s of it embedding 1,055 texts (47 ms per text). BM25 build at 5,000: 7.3 s, 15.6 MB. Estimates:
- Without a cache: about 63,000 texts × 55 ms ≈ 58 min, plus about 1.5 min.
- With eval_out/enterprise_full/emb_cache.sqlite (84 MB, 77,860 entries keyed by model and text) copied to W/emb_cache.sqlite: every base text hits. The 89 extra documents need 1,403 texts (764 sections, 640 records, measured: 1 of 1,404 in the cache), about 1.3 min. Entity and project profile texts whose first-seen document shifts are unmeasured, at most about 5,500 (6.5 min).
- Bank load total with the cache: about 3 to 8 min with the CPUs free. Expect longer while the dry run holds them.
Disk for the new tenant on the compact schema, estimated from the 5,000 tenant's column sizes (halfvec 776 B, no tsv): rows as storage() counts them ≈ sections 67.5 + records 85.3 + documents 4.8 + links 6.0 + BM25 15.6 ≈ 179 MB (about 36 KB per document). On disk with indexes (two 16-bit HNSW about 120 MB per docs/STORAGE.md, GIN, trigram, btree): about 400 to 470 MB (80 to 92 KB per document). WAL: max_wal_size 1 GB and checkpoint_timeout 30 min, with pg_wal at 208 MB now, so a load can add up to about 0.8 GB of WAL before a checkpoint. cie is a superuser, so a manual CHECKPOINT can recycle it. For comparison, the old-schema cie_erb uses 5.6 KB per section row and 6.3 KB per record row, indexes included.
findings.numbers: bank load: about 58 min with no cache, about 3 to 8 min with the cache; tenant about 0.40 to 0.47 GB on disk; free disk 1.8 GB

findings.title: (4) The plain index
findings.detail: Lives in (local or work)/plain/: chunks.jsonl, bm25/ (tantivy, en_stem, written with a 256 MB heap), vectors.npy (fp16, normalised) and meta.json, with a copy of the sizes in work/plain_meta.json. fb50: 499 passages, 1.3 MB folder, BM25 0.4 s, embedding 28.6 s (57 ms per passage; fbtest 70 ms). No plain index has ever been built at 5,000 documents. Estimate from a seeded 600-document sample of mt5k (render plus chunk, no embedding): 7.06 passages per document, so about 35,900 passages and 32.2 MB of passage text. chunks.jsonl about 40 MB; BM25 about 17 MB (0.53 × text, the fb50 ratio); vectors 27.6 MB fp16, 55 MB in RAM as fp32 at evidence time. Read, render and chunk: 0.38 ms per document (about 2 s). The BM25 build takes seconds. Vectors: about 35,900 × 57 to 70 ms ≈ 34 to 42 min, with no cache possible: build_plain calls the embedder directly, and the passage texts differ from the bank's section texts. Plain total at 5,000 ≈ 77 MB as plain_total counts it, about 85 MB on disk.
findings.numbers: about 35,900 passages; about 34 to 42 min to embed; about 85 MB on disk

findings.title: Rest of the pipeline at 5,000 (for planning)
findings.detail: Bank search at 5,000 with BM25: p50 414 ms, p95 838 ms (eval_out/bm25_5k), so evidence for 50 questions takes about 1 min and for all 219 about 3 min, plus the fastembed model load. Fact bank v1 over the same 5,089 documents (Part A dry run, dry5k, whose haystack equals mt5k): 109,528 facts, 106 MB, 11.2 s with a warm disk (152.6 s cold in the u5k probe). v2 with --text-facts: 115 MB, 16 s. ask with v1: about 0.7 to 1.2 s per question at 5,000 (u5k/scale/ans_v1.log). Storage rule 4 at 5,000 by these estimates: about 106 MB for the fact bank against about 182 MB for the bank's rows (ratio about 0.58), so it would fail as it did at 50 documents (0.60). evidence.jsonl is about 96 KB per question (4.8 MB for 50).
findings.numbers: evidence about 1 min per 50 questions; fact bank v1 about 106 MB in 11 to 153 s; rule 4 ratio about 0.58

recommendations: Do not reuse erbfull-5000-9688c2. It would need cie_erb migrated: two migrations that rewrite the sections and records tables of every cie_erb tenant (144k sections, 83k records), need temporary disk, and change a database the reeval scripts use. It would still be contaminated by 3,167 visible bench_loop records and would cover only 11 owners questions.

Load mt5k anew into the current schema, with the same environment as the 50-document run, once the dry run has released the CPUs. Exact sequence (from /home/user/integratedai/cie):
S=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad; W=$S/<partB work>
export CIE_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://cie:cie@localhost:5432/cie_pb CIE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fastembed CIE_LLM_PROVIDER=none CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR=$S/fb_lexical PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONHASHSEED=0
mkdir -p $W && cp $S/mt5k/haystack.json $W/ && ln -s $S/mt5k/index.json $W/index.json && cp <chosen questions.jsonl, e.g. $S/fb50/questions.jsonl> $W/questions.jsonl
cp eval_out/enterprise_full/emb_cache.sqlite $W/emb_cache.sqlite   # 84 MB; all base texts hit
.venv/bin/python -m cie.eval.memory_test load --work $W --workers 3        # new tenant erbfull-5089-xxxxxx, about 3 to 8 min
.venv/bin/python -m cie.eval.memory_test plain --work $W                   # about 35,900 passages, about 35 to 42 min (vectors)
.venv/bin/python -m cie.eval.memory_test evidence --work $W --arms plain-words,plain,bank   # about 1 min per 50 questions
.venv/bin/python -m cie.eval.factbank_test build --work $W                # v1, about 106 MB
.venv/bin/python -m cie.eval.factbank_test ask --work $W
.venv/bin/python -m cie.eval.factbank_test score --work $W
(optional) build --name factbank_v2 --text-facts; ask --name factbank_v2 --lessons $S/fb50/lessons.json
Build the plain index with vectors before running evidence. If evidence runs while vectors.npy is missing, the 'plain' arm is recorded as words only, and the resume logic will not recompute it.

Free disk before loading, or watch it. Projected peak: tenant 0.40 to 0.47 GB, WAL up to +0.8 GB (run CHECKPOINT as cie, a superuser, after the load), cache copy 0.09 GB, plain 0.09 GB, two fact banks 0.22 GB, against 1.8 GB free while Part A's folders keep growing. Options: symlink the fact banks from dry5k if those files are kept, since their haystack equals mt5k; symlink rather than copy the embedding cache; or have the user drop obsolete tenants or databases (for example cie_erb's partial loads, or cie_scale at 7.5 GB). The last one is the user's decision.

Choose the question set knowingly. On the mt5k haystack, all 50 fb50 questions and all 219 eligible mt5k questions (owners 96, deadlines 70, lists 53) have their gold documents inside, and the expected answers were computed over mt5k, so they are exact. Any unseen haystack would have no owners questions: the only owners questions are the benchmark's 100 metadata questions, and all of their gold documents are in mt5k. Deadline and list questions would have to be generated by a script calling memory_test.generate_questions, since no CLI does it.

The repository needs, or Part B's harness must work around: factbank_test.select hard-codes 50 documents, so the work folder is assembled by hand; to_markdown labels the report '50 documents'. A fresh unseen 5,000-document haystack would need the full cost: about 58 min for the bank plus about 35 to 42 min for the plain vectors, about 1.5 to 1.7 h of 4-CPU time.
risks: All times are extrapolations from the Sep 23 load log (18 texts/s), the fb50 load and the plain logs (14 to 17 passages/s), and a 600-document sample. Nothing heavy was run. With the dry run holding the CPUs, real times will be longer.

Not measured: how many entity and project profile texts miss the cache when the 89 extra documents shift batch boundaries. That bound (up to about 5,500 texts, about 6.5 min) is the main uncertainty in the bank-load time with the cache.

Disk is the binding limit (1.8 GB free). WAL can grow to about 1 GB before a checkpoint (checkpoint_timeout is 30 min). Running out of disk mid-load would leave a partial tenant; find_loaded_tenant never picks a partial tenant, so a rerun would start a new load.

The crash on cie_erb is inferred from the code (exact.lookup calls cie_record_tsv outside run_bounded) together with a confirmed missing SQL function. I did not run a Retriever query against cie_erb end to end.

I did not recompute select_docs(seed 5) to prove the tenant equals the benchmark haystack. That rests on the subset and count relations: 5,000 of 5,000 in mt5k, and the 89 missing documents are all metadata or conflicts gold.

I did not check whether HNSW graph differences between the old layout (an expression index on embedding::halfvec) and the new one (a halfvec column) change results. The distances are computed identically.
mt5k is a seen set. fb50, fbtest and mt50 lie inside it, and v2's lessons were trained on fb50's questions, so Part B on mt5k with fb50's questions is optimistic for the fact bank, v2 most of all.

Not checked: the Colab path, the bank+facts and bank+lookup arms, pytest, and the dry5k fact-bank files' persistence (the dry run may overwrite or remove them). Scratch probes I wrote are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/u5kb/pipeline/ (cache_probe.py, plain_probe.py, subset_probe.py, intent_probe.py, and dsids_<tenant>.txt dumps).

reports.summary:
Lens: questions and protocol, read-only. I changed no repository files, ran no pytest and built nothing. My scratch scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/u5kb/questions/ (usage.py, unused.py, used_unused.json, tenant_cov.py, draw_b.py, draw_b_seed*_*.json, ctrl50.py, titles.py, erbfull5000_dsids.txt).

(1) The question pool. mt5k/questions.jsonl has 243 questions. 219 of them are in owners, deadlines or lists and have a checkable expected answer: owners 96 of 100, deadlines 70, lists 53.
- 97 different eligible questions are used elsewhere: fb50 50, fbtest 46 (fbchanged and fbchanged_fixed use the same ids), and mt50 10.
- 122 are unused: owners 47, deadlines 32 (20 Linear due dates, 12 action items), lists 43.
- No other folder holds any of these 219 questions: the md* and u5k sets, the dry runs and the reviews all hold other questions.

(2) Both options are possible. For option (b), the draw can match fb50's mix exactly (26 / 18 / 6, with deadlines split 10 Linear due dates and 8 action items). The lists cannot match fb50's kinds: only 2 pull-request lists are unused, so they would be mostly Linear lists, a kind no fact-bank test has used yet.

Two things block the memory bank arm as things stand:
- **The 5,000-document tenant does not fit.** erbfull-5000-9688c2 holds 5,000 of mt5k's 5,089 documents. 104 of the 219 eligible questions have a gold document among the 89 missing ones, including 85 of the 96 owner questions and 25 of fb50's 26. `find_loaded_tenant` looks for a tenant named erbfull-5089-*, and none exists in any database.
- **That tenant is on an old schema.** cie_erb is at migration f8a9b0c1d2e3. The fb50 bank's database, cie_pb, is at the head (b0c1d2e3f4a5), which adds the compact-storage migration.

So either option needs a new bank of all 5,089 documents built with today's code. A plain index over 5,089 documents is also needed and does not exist yet.

(3) The 50-document control. For option (a) it exists and reproduces: today's v1 gives the same answers as on 2026-10-07 for all 50 questions. For option (b) there is no control; one would have to be built from the union of the gold documents (54 to 73 documents, not 50).

(4) Storage. A rough estimate on the old schema puts v1 at 34.9% of the bank's storage, against a limit of 33.3%. That makes rule 4, and with it "replace", likely to fail again.

My recommendation: make the 50 new questions (option b) the primary set, because they are blind for every arm. Keep fb50's 50 questions (option a) as the secondary set: they are literally the same test, have a ready control, and give the cleanest size effect, but v1 has already been probed on them and they are v2's training questions.

findings.title: Seen status and contamination
findings.detail:
- fb50 and fbtest documents: all 50 of each are inside mt5k.
- mt50 documents: only 17 of 50 are inside mt5k, so 'mt50 lies inside it' holds for 17 documents and 10 questions only.
- v2's lessons (fb50/lessons.json) were trained on fb50's 50 questions and documents, so option (a) is in-sample for v2.
- The questions mt5k generated use v2's training wording: Linear deadline questions say 'due', which is the cue v2 learned. So option (b) does not test v2's known weakness with reworded questions; fbtest did.
- MEMORY_TEST.md says its 5,000-document results are 'to be filled in from the Colab run'. I found no evidence.jsonl for any arm at 5,000 documents, so no arm's evidence on these questions has been seen except v1's probe on fb50.
- Part A's draft (FACTBANK_5K_PREREGISTRATION.md) excludes every mt5k document from its fresh 5,000-document draw (seed 53). All 100 metadata questions have their gold documents in mt5k, so owner questions cannot be drawn from an unseen haystack. Only deadlines and lists could be generated fresh there.
findings.numbers: fb50 50/50, fbtest 50/50, mt50 17/50 documents in mt5k

recommendations: Haystack: mt5k (5,089 documents), disclosed as seen. It is the only haystack where owner questions with checkable answers exist: all 100 benchmark metadata questions have their gold documents there, and Part A's fresh draw excludes them. Do not reuse erbfull-5000-9688c2. Load a new full bank of all 5,089 documents with today's code into a database at migration head b0c1d2e3f4a5, and build the plain index over the same 5,089 documents. Record the load and embedding times.

Primary questions: option (b), 50 new questions from the 122 unused. Fix the seed in the pre-registration (for example 55, after Part A's 53 and 54). Take 26 owners, 18 deadlines (10 Linear due dates and 8 action items, as fb50) and 6 lists. Decide the list rule before drawing. Either (i) order them like `select()`, fewest gold documents first, which keeps fb50's 2-item lists but always yields 4 Linear-by-assignee and 2 Jira; or (ii) draw them seeded and uniform across the 43, which is representative (2 to 10 items, including status and due-window lists). Disclose that the kinds differ from fb50's 5 pull-request and 1 Jira lists either way, because only 2 pull-request lists are unused. Freeze the question file's sha256 and save only counts.

Control for (b): build a small set from the union of the 50 questions' gold documents (54 to 73 documents depending on the list rule, so not 50). Check that every expected answer is unchanged within it, as Part A does. Run every arm on both sets. This costs a bank load of about 1 to 2 minutes, about 30 to 60 s of plain-index embedding, and under a second per fact-bank build.

Secondary questions: option (a), fb50's 50 questions at 5,089 documents, literally 'the same test'. Its 50-document control already exists for every arm: v1 reproduces exactly, and bank, plain-words, plain and v2 are stored. Still, re-collect the bank's 50-document evidence from erbfull-50-c6dd93 in cie_pb in the same run, so both sizes use the same code. Label v1 on (a) as already probed (0.226 / 0.402 / 0.745, own answers 0.846), and v2 on (a) as in-sample, trained on these exact questions.

Arms: plain-words, plain and bank (the present bank, default search) as references, plus fact bank v1 (factbank.sqlite, untrained) and fact bank v2 (factbank_v2.sqlite built with --text-facts, asked with fb50/lessons.json, sha256 afa4e7d9fee0a05c…). The rules decide on v1, the system the original rules were written for. v2 is scored against the same rules as a secondary result and decides nothing.

Rules on the primary set at 5,089 documents, with the original thresholds unchanged. Means are over the three groups. (1) v1 − bank ≥ −0.03 in every group at 24,000 characters. (2) v1 − bank ≥ +0.10 on the mean at 2,000 characters. (3) v1's own answers ≥ 0.70 on the mean. (4) v1's SQLite file is at most a third of the bank's storage (rows plus BM25, both on the current schema, same 5,089 documents). New rule 5, own answers hold at size: v1's own answers at 5,089 documents ≥ v1's on the control − 0.05, as in Part A rule 1. Also reported, with no threshold: each arm's change from the control at 2,000, 6,000 and 24,000 characters, by group and mean; the fact bank's change minus the bank's change; and fact bank against plain-words, the strongest reference at 50 documents.

What decides: 'Replace' exactly as originally written, meaning rules 1, 2 and 4 all met on the primary set at 5,089 documents. Rules 3 and 5 say whether its own answers hold. Pre-register the outcome where rules 1 and 2 are met but rule 4 is not: the result is 'not decided', as at 50 documents, and storage is not judged against a new bar inside Part B. The original results say any new storage rule must be set before a smaller layout is built. Rule 1 met but rule 2 not met: the lead near the top does not survive size; diagnose per question. Rule 1 not met: the present bank stays.

Report: the full `factbank_test.to_markdown` table per arm, budget and group for both sets and both sizes; own answers for v1 and v2; every question whose result changes between sizes; search time (median, 90th percentile, maximum); build and load times; storage, broken down by part; the checker; journal replays; contradictions and stale counts; how many questions were drawn and set aside; and the probe's numbers alongside the run's. State how fine the measures are: one question moves a group by 0.038 (owners), 0.056 (deadlines) or up to 0.167 (lists). Rule 1's −0.03 is less than one owner or deadline question.

Original rules that cannot be applied as written at 5,000 documents: (a) 'storage for these 50 documents' becomes storage for 5,089, and the bank must be on the current schema; (b) the original had no 50-document control, so 'the change from 50 to 5,000' is new and needs a control per set; (c) `select()`'s 50-document limit cannot hold for new questions, which need 54 to 73 documents; (d) the bank arm cannot reuse any existing tenant; (e) rule 1's margin can only be read as 'no question lost' in two groups.
risks: What I could not verify: the probe's 5,000-document numbers (0.226 / 0.402 / 0.745, own answers 0.846). Their outputs are not in u5k/protocol/orig5k, and I did not rebuild the 106 MB bank to recompute them, so I have no breakdown by group.

What I did not check: whether today's search code runs at all against cie_erb's older schema; how many passages a 5,089-document plain index would hold, or how much of it the embedding caches already cover; how long a 5,089-document load would take now.

What I did not check: whether owner questions become ambiguous at 5,089 documents. They describe a document instead of naming it, and the 5,000-document load found 45 near-duplicate pairs. I checked only the deadline titles (all unique).

What I did not check: how v1 and v2 handle Linear lists by status and by due window on real questions. The original results say only unit tests cover them, and option (b)'s lists will mostly be of these kinds.

Rule 4 will probably fail again: v1 is about 34.9% of the old-schema bank, and a current-schema bank is smaller. So 'replace' is probably undecidable whatever happens on rules 1 and 2. The pre-registration should state that before the run.

The 5,089-document haystack is a seen set, and the question pool comes from the same memory-test set as fb50 and fbtest. Part A's draw excludes every mt5k document, so there is no unseen haystack for owner questions anywhere in the benchmark.

Option (a) is no longer blind: v1 has been probed on it, and it is v2's training set. Option (b) uses the training wording for generated questions, so it overstates how v2 would do on reworded questions.

Small groups: 6 list questions decide a third of every mean. In option (b) a draw with lists of 2 to 10 items can swing the lists group by about 0.17 per question. Pick the list rule before drawing, not after seeing the sizes.
The bank's 50-document evidence is from 2026-10-07. The bank code has not changed since 2026-10-05 (checked in git), but I did not re-run the evidence.

reports.summary: Storage and evidence lens for Part B (read-only; no bank built, nothing loaded, no repository file changed). (1) Rule 4 is not met at 5,000 documents in any of the four ways I measured it. The fact bank takes 0.35 to 0.64 of the bank's storage, and the rule needs at most 0.333. On the bank layout the 50-document test used (16-bit halfvec vectors, no stored tsvector, measured in cie_pb), the bank's own rows plus its BM25 index come to about 179 MB at 5,000 documents. That makes fact bank v1 (106.0 MB) 0.58 to 0.59 of the bank and v2 (115.0 MB) 0.63 to 0.64, almost exactly the 50-document ratios (0.597 and 0.642). The only 5k tenant, erbfull-5000-9688c2 in cie_erb, sits two migrations behind head (f8a9b0c1d2e3: 32-bit vectors plus stored tsvector). Its bank_total is 303.9 MB as it stands, which would make v1 look like 0.349. That tenant also holds 4,580 records left by loop-benchmark runs, and it holds 5,000 documents rather than mt5k's 5,089, so find_loaded_tenant would not reuse it anyway. (2) The evidence is built with fixed constants that do not depend on the haystack size: a 24,000-character budget, K=60, passages of about 1,000 characters, bank items cut to a 300-character summary and 1,500-character detail, and the fact bank's own 24,000 budget. Each arm is scored on text[:b] for b = 2,000, 6,000 and 24,000, so 'answer within 2,000 chars' is defined the same way at 5k. But it only checks that the answer string is present, not which document it came from. At 5k every deadline question's expected date appears in 3 to 95 unrelated documents (median 35 for Linear due dates), so chance hits grow with size. (3) Search time p50 at 50 documents: plain-words 0.6 ms, plain 10.6 ms, bank 149.9 ms, fact bank v1 5.38 ms (v2 72.6 ms). Expected at 5k: bank about 414 ms p50 / 838 ms p95 (BM25 test A), fact bank v1 about 0.75 s (design probe; 0.46 s of that is named()). So the fact bank goes from 28 times faster to roughly 2 times slower. (4) The named() cost is Python's regex cache (512 patterns) overflowing on 7,929 aliases: 461.8 ms per call against 19.2 ms if the patterns were compiled once. The memory test's question generator already drops reused Linear and Jira keys and pull request numbers, so none of fb50's questions is affected. But 10 of mt5k's 53 list questions have expected lists that leave out a real item whose key is reused.

findings.title: How memory_test computes bank_total and plain_total
findings.detail: cie/src/cie/eval/memory_test.py storage() (lines 865-879). bank_total adds sum(pg_column_size(x.*)) over the tenant's rows in documents, sections, memory_records, record_links and section_facts, plus the size of the tenant's tantivy BM25 directory (cie.retrieval.bm25.tenant_dir). It leaves out every PostgreSQL index, because the docstring treats them as shared by all tenants: the HNSW indexes, the trigram and tsv GIN indexes and the B-trees. It also leaves out page and TOAST-chunk overhead. pg_column_size of a whole row decompresses every field when any field is stored out of line, so it is closer to the logical row size than to the bytes on disk. plain_total adds plain_meta.json's text_bytes (the passages' UTF-8 text), bm25_bytes (the tantivy directory) and vector_bytes (vectors.npy, 16-bit). Rule 4 uses only bank_total. The default search reads exactly the counted tables (graph expansion in mode 'rem' uses record_links, not the rem_* tables) plus indexes that are not counted.
findings.numbers: Tables counted: 5, plus the BM25 directory. Indexes counted: 0.

findings.title: How factbank_build.json 'bytes' is computed
findings.detail: cie/src/cie/factbank/bank.py build() line 256: path.stat().st_size of the SQLite file after the inserts. findings.title: How the evidence arms are built (memory_test evidence --arms plain-words,plain,bank)
findings.detail: collect_evidence (memory_test.py 789-862). plain-words: tantivy BM25 (en_stem, title boost) top K=60 of the raw documents rendered as 'field: value' and cut by bench_enterprise.chunk into passages of about 1,000 characters. plain: reciprocal-rank fusion (c=60) of the BM25 top 60 and a brute-force cosine top 60 over 16-bit fastembed vectors. bank: Retriever.retrieve(question, admin, company) with its defaults (packet_token_budget 12,000, graph budget 4*log2(N)), blocks '(source, type) summary[:300]' plus 'detail[:1500]'; a search that fails is recorded as an empty packet with bank_error. Every arm goes through fill(budget=EVIDENCE_CHARS=24,000), which numbers the blocks '[n] head', joins them with blank lines and drops the first block that does not fit. The fact bank (engine.FactBank.evidence, budget 24,000) gives fact blocks per entity, best first, then the seed documents' text at up to 6,000 characters each. Its accounting undercounts a little: at fb50 the median length is 24,021 and the maximum 24,148. v2 is cut to exactly 24,000 and starts with a 'Most likely answers' block. factbank_test.score cuts every arm to text[:b] for b in 2,000, 6,000 and 24,000 and calls reachable(). So the definition does not change at 5k. Chance hits do rise with size, because reachable() only tests that the string is there (finding below). At 50 documents I checked how much of each arm's reach comes from a block titled with the gold document: plain arms 100%; fact bank 0.767→0.667 at 2k and 0.987→0.956 at 24k; bank 0.630→0.506 at 24k. The bank's block heads show a record summary rather than the title, so its figure is a lower bound.
findings.numbers: fb50 evidence length p50: plain-words 23,524, plain 23,530, bank 23,608, fact bank 24,021. Blocks per question p50: plain 24, bank 32. First block p50: plain about 975 chars, bank 853, fact bank 543. bank_error 0 of 50.

findings.title: Why named() is slow at 5k: the regex cache overflows
findings.detail: engine.FactBank.named builds re.search(r'(?<![\w-])'+re.escape(alias)+r'(?![\w-])') for every alias on every call. Python 3.12.3 keeps 512 compiled patterns (re._MAXCACHE), so above 512 aliases every call compiles every pattern again. I reproduced this with synthetic aliases: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/u5kb/storage/named_cost.py. The code is frozen, so this can only be reported. Separately, fb50's alias table has 49 one-word aliases, including first names from action items ('alex', 'daniel', 'diego'). Any question containing such a name seeds that person. At 5k this may crowd the fact bank's first 2,000 characters; that is a hypothesis I did not test.
findings.numbers: 215 aliases: 2.3 ms per call (0.50 ms with patterns compiled once). 7,929 aliases: 461.8 ms per call (19.2 ms compiled once, 24 times faster).

findings.title: Reused keys and ambiguous expected answers
findings.detail: The memory test's question generator does handle reuse. memory_test.generate_questions drops, through unique(), every Linear or Jira document whose key appears more than once in the haystack and every GitHub document whose PR number repeats. linear_due and action_due also need a unique title, and action items need a unique (owner, task) within their meeting. The check itself (check, reachable) does nothing about duplicates. In mt5k: 9 Linear keys reused (20 documents), 3 Jira keys (9 documents), 2 PR numbers (4 documents). fb50's 6 list questions are untouched: none of their people owns a dropped document (dupcheck.py). Across mt5k, though, the dropped documents leave 10 of 53 list questions with an expected list that misses a real matching item. Those questions would cost an arm precision on its own answers (direct F1) but not reach. Owners questions come from the benchmark and are never filtered: metadata-qst_0034's gold document is a Slack channel titled 'customer-success', a title 120 mt5k documents share, but its answer INC-2034 appears in no other document. One cosmetic point: factbank_test.to_markdown hard-codes '50 documents' in its heading.

recommendations: Fix the bank's storage layout in the Part B pre-registration: measure bank_total on a tenant in a database at head migration b0c1d2e3f4a5 (halfvec, no stored tsvector), as fb50 and fbtest were (cie_pb). Do not measure it in cie_erb (f8a9b0c1d2e3) or in 'cie' (e7f8a9b0c1d2). The layout alone moves rule 4 for v1 from about 0.58 to about 0.35.

Load a fresh tenant holding exactly mt5k's 5,089 documents. Do not reuse erbfull-5000-9688c2: it lacks 89 of the documents (25 of them fb50's), it carries 4,580 loop-run records and 1,386 links that would both enter search and inflate bank_total by about 13.9 MB, and its BM25 outbox has 3,685 pending rows.

Pre-state the expected outcome of rule 4: not met (0.58 to 0.64 on head layout). Report bank_total by table, the fact bank's dbstat breakdown at 5k, and a second view with indexes counted on both sides (the bank's indexes, roughly 111 MB, against the fact bank's own index pages, about 26%), clearly labelled as for information.

Because 'answer within N chars' only tests that the answer string is present, report next to it, for information, the share that comes from a block of a gold document. Plain blocks carry the title; the bank's evidence would need the document id, which bank_blocks does not keep. Also report, for each question, how many unrelated documents carry the answer (chance.json). Pay most attention to the deadline group and to owners questions with common answers ('pass', '2026-04', 'Maya Chen').

Report search time per arm with p50, p90 and maximum at 5k. State beforehand that the fact bank is expected to be slower than the bank (about 0.75 s against about 0.41 s p50) and that 0.46 s of it is named() recompiling 7,929 regexes. Record the 19 ms a compile-once version takes as a note for the future, not a change, since the code is frozen.

If Part B draws questions beyond fb50 from mt5k, exclude or flag the 10 list questions whose expected list misses an item with a reused key (linear_assignee-002/-015, linear_status-004/-005, linear_due_window-003/-007/-008, jira_assignee-001/-002/-004), or score them on reach only.
Patch the report heading in the Part B write-up, not in the frozen code: to_markdown always prints '50 documents'.
risks: If the bank were measured in cie_erb's old layout, v1 would land at 0.349 to 0.366, about 5-10% above the one-third bar. A small change in the fact bank's size, such as leaving out the 89 extra documents, could then flip rule 4 to 'met' for a reason that has nothing to do with the fact bank.
bank_total leaves out every PostgreSQL index while the fact bank's bytes include its SQLite indexes (about 26%). The comparison stays tilted against the fact bank at 5k, as it was at 50 documents.

The reach measure's chance hits grow with the haystack: every deadline date also appears in 3-95 unrelated mt5k documents. At 24,000 characters every arm may look better than it is, and the arms will look closer together.
Timing at 5k was or will be measured on a shared 4-core machine during a CPU-heavy dry run. Absolute milliseconds, especially the bank's, may be inflated and noisy.
A load into a database behind head may fail or give a mixed layout (32-bit vectors with a NULL tsvector). I did not check this.
The head-layout bank size at 5k (179.2 MB) is a projection. It matches fb50's measured bytes per row to about 1.3% for sections, but no 5k bank on head layout was measured.

critic.summary:
Completeness critique of the three Part B reports. I changed no repository files, built nothing and ran no pytest; I only ran quick reads and queries.

**Where the three lenses agree, and I confirmed it:**
- No existing tenant can be reused. erbfull-5000-9688c2 is missing 89 of mt5k's documents, is two migrations behind, and is contaminated. Part B needs a new load of all 5,089 documents into a database at head.
- Rule 4 cannot be met. On the head layout the fact bank is 0.58 to 0.64 of the bank, against a limit of 0.333. So "Replace" is effectively decided in advance as "not decided".
- No retrieval, memory, ingest, eval or memory_test code has changed since the 50-document run (`git log 8375901..HEAD` on those paths is empty).

**Six problems the reports miss or get wrong:**
1. **The probe's 5,000-document numbers cannot be traced to any file.** No file under u5k holds 0.226, 0.402 or 0.745. The only 0.846 is a different measure: own answers on 157 clean multi-document questions in u5k/ambiguity/ask.log. The "0.75 s per question" timing comes from u5k/scale/ans_v1.jsonl, which holds Part A's multi-document question kinds, not fb50's.
2. **The recommended seed-55 draw contains flawed list questions.** It includes jira_assignee-002 and linear_due_window-003, which the storage lens showed have incomplete expected lists. The kind-matched draws include jira_assignee-001, -002 and -004. Seed 7 and seed 55 have also already been drawn and their makeup inspected, so the seed must be disclosed or replaced.
3. **The bank's search has hidden time limits.** Entity matching gives up after 400 ms and the lexical tiers after 1.5 or 4 s. When a limit is hit, it is logged only at DEBUG level and the result is silently empty. Under the current CPU load, the bank's evidence at 5,000 documents could lose results without any visible error.
4. **A failed bank search counts as a zero and is never retried.** score() treats the empty text left by bank_error as a miss, and the resume logic will not recompute it.
5. **The control's conditions have changed.** The 50-document control evidence was collected on Oct 7, when erbfull-50-c6dd93 was the only tenant in cie_pb. cie_pb now holds 6 small tenants, and loading 5,089 more documents into it would change the shared indexes and query plans the control searches.
6. **"Seen" applies to both systems, not just the fact bank.** The present bank's BM25 and passage-expansion work was evaluated on the same 5,000-document base: the gold documents of the benchmark's 500 questions plus a seed-5 sample.

**Decisions the reports leave open:**
- **Haystack.** mt5k is what the original docs promised and it is cheap to load with the cache. An unseen option nobody considered: Part A's seed-53 draw plus the planted gold documents of the owner questions. That is about 1.5 to 1.7 hours of CPU, and disk cannot hold both.
- **Which fact bank decides.** v1, v2, or v13, the current system. ask_plans gives v3 to v14 evidence text, so v13 can be scored the same way.
- **Primary question set.** fb50's questions or 50 new ones, with exclusions fixed before drawing.
- **Plain keyword search.** Whether the fact bank against plain-words is a rule or only reported. Plain-words led at 50 documents, and that was the original reason for testing at 5,000.
- **What a rule-2 pass means.** A pass can come from the bank collapsing rather than the fact bank holding up.
- **Disk.** 1.7 GB is free now, against a projected peak of 1.2 to 1.7 GB. pg_wal is on the same disk, so running out stops all of Postgres, not just this load.
- **New test code.** select() is fixed at 50 documents, score() only scores factbank.jsonl, measure() has no 6,000 budget, and the report title always says 50 documents. Part A's draft also points to a Part B pre-registration (FACTBANK_5K_B_PREREGISTRATION.md) that does not exist yet.

findings.title: Probe numbers for v1 on fb50 at 5k are unverifiable and possibly conflated
findings.detail: I searched u5k, dry5k* and audit_* for 0.402 and found nothing. u5k/protocol/orig5k holds only haystack.json, index.json and questions.jsonl: no factbank.jsonl and no report. The only 0.846 in u5k is in u5k/ambiguity/ask.log: 'clean n=157 mean own_score=0.846'. That is multi-document planner questions (action_owner_issues, person_count, ticket_link...), not fb50's owners, deadlines and lists. Separately, the storage lens's '~0.75 s per FactBank.ask (u5k/scale/ans_v1.jsonl)' comes from Part A kinds (action_owner_issues-081, compare_two-186...), not fb50 kinds. The cost is dominated by named(), so the order of magnitude probably carries over, but it was not measured on these questions. Consequences: the design probe's 'answer within 2,000/6,000/24,000 chars 0.226/0.402/0.745, own 0.846' cannot be cited as fact in the pre-registration. The questions lens's derived threshold ('rule 2 on (a) needs bank@2k ≤ 0.126') rests on it.
findings.numbers: 0 files containing 0.226/0.402/0.745; the single 0.846 is n=157 multi-doc own-score

findings.title: Contradiction: the recommended option (b) draws include list questions with broken expected answers
findings.detail: The questions lens recommends seed 55 with lists drawn uniformly. The storage lens lists 10 mt5k list questions whose expected list leaves out a real item with a reused key: linear_assignee-002/-015, linear_status-004/-005, linear_due_window-003/-007/-008, jira_assignee-001/-002/-004. I intersected the saved draws. draw_b_seed55_plain.json includes jira_assignee-002 and linear_due_window-003. draw_b_seed55_kindmatch.json includes jira_assignee-002 and -004. draw_b_seed7_kindmatch.json includes jira_assignee-001. The 'fewest gold documents first' draws (both seeds) and seed7_plain include none. These questions would cost every arm direct F1 (a real item counts as a false positive) but not reach. Also, seeds 7 and 55 were already drawn, and their kinds and gold-document counts inspected, before any seed was fixed.
findings.numbers: seed55_plain: 2 flawed of 6 lists; seed55_kindmatch: 2; seed7_kindmatch: 1

findings.title: Bank evidence can be degraded silently by machine load (hidden time limits)
findings.detail: exact.py runs the fuzzy entity match (trigram similarity over entity summaries) through run_bounded with 400 ms. lexical.py's tiers are bounded at TIER_MS 4,000 and PARTIAL_TIER_MS 1,500. On a timeout, run_bounded returns None and logs only at log.debug (retrieval/bounded.py). Nothing reaches evidence.jsonl. At 50 documents these never time out. At 5,089 documents (about 34k records), with a CPU-heavy dry run holding all 4 cores, the 400 ms bound in particular could cut the bank's entity seeds for some questions. The bank's evidence would then depend on machine load, not on its design, and only the bank arm is exposed to this. None of the three reports mentions it.
findings.numbers: limits: ent_sim 400 ms, lexical tier 4,000 / 1,500 ms; logged at DEBUG only

findings.title: Failed bank searches become permanent zeros
findings.detail: collect_evidence catches every exception from retriever.retrieve and records bank_error with an empty 'bank' string. score() then scores '' as reach 0 (it skips only None). The resume logic counts a row as done once every arm key exists, so a transient failure is never retried. Examples: Postgres restarting after a disk-full PANIC, or a lock or timeout. The pipeline lens noted the same trap for the plain arm when vectors.npy is missing (it silently falls back to words only), but not for the bank.
findings.numbers: bank_error was 0 of 50 at fb50; no check at 5k

findings.title: The 50-document control was collected with its tenant alone in cie_pb, and it would not be after the 5k load
findings.detail: cie_pb now holds 6 tenants: erbfull-50-c6dd93 (created 03:27 on Oct 7, just before commit 8375901 at 03:32), plus 1e4908, d85f0c, d10d57, 4dd4d4 and a96489, all created 05:01 to 05:35. So the stored fb50 bank evidence was collected when c6dd93 was the only tenant. The HNSW index and the trigram and tsv GIN indexes are shared across tenants. Vector search uses iterative scan (relaxed_order, max_scan_tuples 40,000, ef_search ≥ 100). Loading about 34k sections and 34k records into cie_pb would put the 50-document tenant at roughly 1.3% of the index and change planner statistics for the bounded queries. The control's re-collected evidence may then differ from Oct 7 for reasons unrelated to the fact bank. The questions lens recommends re-collecting the control 'in the same run', but not when (before or after the load) or where.
findings.numbers: cie_pb: 6 tenants, about 2.8k sections, 61 MB, alembic b0c1d2e3f4a5, pgvector 0.8.1

findings.title: mt5k is seen for both systems, not only for the fact bank
findings.detail: MEMORY_TEST_PREREGISTRATION.md: the base is every gold document of the benchmark's 500 questions plus a source-stratified sample (seed 5), plus the metadata gold documents. BM25_RESULTS.md test A, and the expansion ('right document, wrong part') work, were measured on that same local 5,000-document bank with those 500 questions. The reports frame 'seen' as favouring the fact bank (fb50 inside mt5k, v2 trained on fb50, v1 already probed). The present bank's search design was also tuned on this haystack, though not on the 100 metadata questions. Both should be disclosed. It also means the original promise ('the same test on the 5,000-document haystack') literally names this seen haystack.
findings.numbers: base = gold of 500 benchmark questions + seed-5 sample; erbfull-5000 = mt5k minus 89 planted gold

findings.title: An unseen-haystack option was dismissed too quickly
findings.detail: The questions lens concludes that owner questions cannot come from an unseen haystack, because all 100 metadata questions have their gold documents in mt5k and Part A's draw excludes mt5k. But mt5k itself was built as a base plus planted metadata gold. The same construction works on Part A's fresh seed-53 draw: the 5,000 unseen documents, plus the gold documents of the 26 owner questions drawn from the 47 unused ones. Deadlines and lists would be generated over it with memory_test.generate_questions. That gives unseen distractors for both systems. Costs: no embedding-cache hits (about 58 min for the bank load plus 35 to 42 min for plain vectors), dependence on Part A's draw, which is still a draft, and about 0.45 GB more disk, which rules out also loading mt5k. It is a real choice to make and disclose, not a non-option.
findings.numbers: about 1.5 to 1.7 h of 4-CPU time vs about 3 to 8 min with the cache on mt5k

findings.title: Which fact bank is 'the fact bank' is undecided, and the current system is missing as an arm
findings.detail: Part A tests 'the current system' (v4 to v14, decisive v13). The Part B reports consider only v1 (untrained) and v2 (single-fact lessons). factbank_multi.ask_plans gives v3 to v14 a full 24,000-character evidence text (a plan head plus TrainedBank evidence), so v13 can be scored on reach exactly like the other arms. If the product candidate is v13, a Part B decided on v1 tests a superseded system. If the rules stay on v1 for continuity, v13 should be a pre-declared secondary arm. Cost at 5k: about 4.3 s per question (u5k/protocol/cmp.out, w5k v13 median 4,308 ms), so about 4 min for 50 questions. Caveat: v13's lessons include fb50/lessons.json, so it is in-sample on option (a).
findings.numbers: v13 at 5k: median 4.3 s, p90 7.2 s per question (multi-doc probe)

findings.title: Rule 4 makes 'Replace' predetermined; the headline needs redefining before the run
findings.detail: Storage and pipeline agree: on the head layout, v1 is 0.58 to 0.59 and v2 0.63 to 0.64 of bank_total. The questions lens's 34.9% / 37.8% is the old cie_erb layout, and the storage lens shows the layout alone moves v1 from about 0.58 to about 0.35. That figure must not appear as the estimate. With rule 4 certain to fail, 'Replace' cannot be met whatever happens on rules 1 and 2. FACTBANK_RESULTS.md says any new storage bar must be set before a smaller layout is built, so Part B should not move the bar. It therefore has to say in advance what its own result is, for example 'the evidence lead holds at size' (rules 1 and 2), and how each case is read. Two cases need care. (i) Rule 2 can pass because the bank collapses (e.g. v1 0.23 against bank 0.12), with both arms poor near the top. (ii) Plain-words beating the fact bank at 5k: the original results named plain-words as the open question ('whether the fact bank holds up when search is hard').
findings.numbers: head layout: v1 0.581 to 0.592, v2 0.631 to 0.642; old layout 0.349 to 0.397; limit 0.333

findings.title: Harness gaps that need new, separate code (consistent with Part A's freeze)
findings.detail: factbank_test: select() hard-codes N_DOCS=50 and LIST_DOCS=20. score() reads only factbank.jsonl and factbank_build.json, so v2 or v13 cannot be scored by it without separate work folders. measure() and compare() score only the 2,000 and 24,000 budgets, not 6,000. to_markdown prints '50 documents'. bank_blocks keeps no document id, so a 'from a gold document' variant of reach cannot be computed for the bank without new collection code. Part A's draft freezes 'every existing function in cie/src/cie/eval' and points to docs/FACTBANK_5K_B_PREREGISTRATION.md, which does not exist. So Part B needs its own new module and run script, committed before the run.
findings.numbers: N_DOCS=50, LIST_DOCS=20, BUDGETS used by measure: 2,000 and 24,000 only

findings.title: Disk: no margin, and running out risks the whole Postgres cluster
findings.detail: df shows 1.7 GB free now (the pipeline lens said 1.8). /var/lib/postgresql/16/main is on the same filesystem. max_wal_size is 1 GB, checkpoint_timeout 30 min, and pg_wal is 208 MB. The pipeline lens's projected peak is 1.2 to 1.7 GB: tenant 0.40 to 0.47 GB, WAL up to +0.8 GB, cache 0.09 GB, plain 0.09 GB, fact banks 0.22 GB. A full disk during a WAL write makes PostgreSQL PANIC, which takes down every database, not just the load. Part A's dry run is writing to the same disk. Symlinking dry5k's fact banks (the pipeline lens's idea) saves 0.2 GB but ties Part B to files another run is still writing.
findings.numbers: free 1.7 GB; projected peak 1.2 to 1.7 GB; max_wal_size 1 GB

findings.title: Reach becomes less discriminating at 5k, and some owner answers are near-meaningless as reach
findings.detail: The storage lens's chance.json, which I spot-checked: every fb50 deadline date appears in unrelated mt5k documents (linear_due median 35, maximum 95). Owner answers such as '2026-03-13' (metadata-qst_0095) appear in 115 other documents, and 'pass' in 865. reachable() tests only that the string is present. So at 24,000 characters, the budget rule 1 is judged on, arms that pack in many documents pick up chance hits, and the arms look closer together. Rule 1's −0.03 margin is smaller than one owner question (0.038) or one deadline question (0.056). A single chance hit or miss can decide it.
findings.numbers: one question moves owners by 0.038, deadlines by 0.056, lists by up to 0.167

findings.title: Settings and seeds of the 50-document run were not recorded
findings.detail: There is no cie/.env (only .env.example), so the settings are code defaults plus environment variables. The fb50 folder has no record of the environment. I confirmed CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR=<scratchpad>/fb_lexical indirectly: it holds exactly cie_pb's 6 tenant directories, including 06a6e697 = c6dd93. PYTHONHASHSEED is set by Part A and in the pipeline lens's commands, but the Oct 7 run almost certainly did not set it. If any retrieval tie-break iterates over a set, the re-collected control can differ from the stored one for that reason alone.
findings.numbers: settings that matter: lexical_engine bm25, packet_token_budget 12,000, graph_budget_coefficient 4.0, LLM none

recommendations: Decide the haystack explicitly and write the reason down. Either (A) mt5k, the literal promise: cheap with the embedding cache, owners included, disclosed as seen for both systems; or (B) Part A's seed-53 draw plus the planted gold documents of the drawn owner questions: unseen distractors, about 1.5 to 1.7 h of CPU, and it must wait for Part A's freeze. Disk rules out doing both.

Decide which fact bank decides. Keep the original rules on v1 for continuity. Pre-declare v2 and v13 as secondary arms, scored on the same reach budgets (2,000/6,000/24,000) and own answers, each labelled in-sample where it is: v2 and v13 on fb50.

Primary question set. If option (b), apply these before drawing: exclude the 10 list questions with incomplete expected lists; fix the list rule (fewest gold documents first, or uniform); fix how owner questions with very common answers are handled (for example, flag those whose answer appears in more than 50 other documents, and report reach with and without them); check the drawn owners' gold documents against the load's 45 near-duplicate pairs. Use a seed that has not been drawn yet, or disclose that seeds 7 and 55 were drawn and their makeup inspected. Freeze the question file's sha256. Keep option (a) as the secondary set, with v1 labelled 'probed' and v2 and v13 labelled in-sample.

Do not cite the probe's 0.226/0.402/0.745 and 0.846 as results. No file holds them, and the only 0.846 is a different measure. Either reproduce v1 on fb50 at 5k inside the frozen run (build about 11 to 150 s, ask about 1 min) and report it as a run step, or call them 'recalled, files deleted'. Re-derive the rule-2 threshold the questions lens computed from them.

Load the 5,089-document tenant into a fresh database migrated to head (b0c1d2e3f4a5), not into cie_pb, so that each size's tenant is alone in its indexes, as c6dd93 was on Oct 7. Re-collect the 50-document control evidence in cie_pb under the frozen environment, before anything else. Diff it against the Oct 7 evidence.jsonl and report any change. Use the re-collected file as the control.

Integrity gates, pre-registered as 'rerun, not score' conditions: 0 bank_error rows (delete and recollect any that occur); plain_meta shows vectors for every passage before evidence runs; the same document set in the bank tenant, the plain index and both fact banks (compare counts and dsid sets); a settings dump (get_settings().model_dump(), with secrets removed) identical between the control and the 5k run; PYTHONHASHSEED=0 everywhere; the cie.retrieval.bounded logger set to DEBUG in the new harness (this changes no repository file), with the number of give-ups per arm and size reported and required to be 0, or the question rerun with the CPUs free.

Collect bank evidence and all timings only when nothing else is running: after Part A's dry run, with a warm-up pass. Then run the bank evidence a second time and require identical text, or report every difference. State in advance that absolute times are from a shared 4-core machine.

Rules and decision text. Keep rules 1 to 4 and their thresholds unchanged. Pre-state that rule 4 will not be met (v1 about 0.58 to 0.59 on the head layout), so 'Replace' cannot be met. Name Part B's headline as 'the evidence lead holds at size': rules 1 and 2 against the bank, plus a new rule 5, own answers at 5k ≥ control − 0.05. Pre-state how each case is read: rule 2 met with both arms low at 2,000 characters; plain-words ahead of the fact bank at 5k; rule 1 failing by one question. Report fact bank minus plain-words at each budget, with no threshold unless one is chosen now. Note that the model-answering check on Colab is still owed, whatever Part B finds.

Add a secondary reach measure that counts the answer only when it comes from a gold document's block, for every arm. The new harness must keep source ids for the bank's blocks. Report the count of unrelated documents carrying each answer (chance.json) next to reach.

Write the Part B harness as a new module plus a frozen run script, committed with the pre-registration before any 5k evidence is collected. It needs to: select or assemble the work folder beyond 50 documents; score v1, v2 and v13 at 2,000/6,000/24,000; label the report with the real document count; keep bank block source ids; and run the integrity gates. Create docs/FACTBANK_5K_B_PREREGISTRATION.md, which Part A already references.

Disk plan before loading: do not copy dry5k files; rebuild the fact banks in Part B's own folder and record their sha256. Symlink, don't copy, the embedding cache. Run CHECKPOINT as cie every few minutes during the load. Watch df and abort the load below about 400 MB free. Freeing space elsewhere (cie_erb's partial tenants, cie_scale) is the user's decision.

Record provenance: the embedding cache's source and fastembed/onnxruntime versions (spot-check a few cached vectors against freshly computed ones), the load and plain-index times, and the git commit. Report storage by part (the bank's tables plus BM25; the fact bank's dbstat), with an index-inclusive view of both sides for information.
risks: If Part B runs on mt5k with fb50's questions as the primary set, the fact bank's side is largely known in advance (v1 probed, v2 and v13 in-sample) and only the bank arm is blind. Any rule-2 outcome there invites the objection that it was chosen after looking.

If the bank's evidence is collected while the dry run holds the CPUs, the 400 ms entity-match limit and the 1.5 to 4 s lexical limits can silently cut the bank's results. The bank would look worse because of load. This bias works only against the bank.
Running out of disk during the load can PANIC the shared Postgres cluster, which also holds cie_pb (the control tenants) and cie_erb. Free space is 1.7 GB against a projected peak of up to 1.7 GB.

The re-collected 50-document control may not reproduce the Oct 7 bank evidence: 5 tenants have been added to cie_pb since, PYTHONHASHSEED differs, and shared indexes and statistics may change. The 'change from 50 to 5,000' could be partly an artefact unless the control is re-collected under frozen conditions and compared.

Rule 1 at 24,000 characters is decided by one question in owners or deadlines, and chance hits grow with the haystack. The rule-1 outcome may reflect string coincidences rather than finding the right document, unless the gold-attributed variant is reported.

Option (b) lists drawn uniformly can include questions with incomplete expected lists (verified in 3 of the 6 saved draws), and lists of up to 10 items. With 6 list questions making up a third of every mean, one list can move the mean by about 0.056.

Rule 4 will not be met, so 'Replace' is decided before the run. Without a pre-stated headline, the write-up will be tempted to move the storage bar or reinterpret afterwards, which the original results explicitly ruled out.

What I did not verify: the storage lens's chance counts beyond a spot check of chance.json; whether today's code would actually raise on cie_erb (moot if it is not used); near-duplicate ambiguity among owner gold documents; whether the iterative HNSW scan actually changes the 50-document tenant's results after a large load. I only infer the risk from the shared-index layout and the settings in vector.py.
Scratch: I wrote no files. Checks were read-only queries of cie_pb, git log, and greps of the scratchpad folders u5k, u5kb, fb50 and fb_lexical.
